correctness.rationale: For every odd n >= 3, parity-reindexing gives a bijection between source states and cyclic edge-AND assignments. Forced boundary bits and independent-set enumeration give the exact Fibonacci factor per maximal zero run, while the two constant outputs yield Lucas(n) and one predecessor. The antitone-Galois argument proves F^3=F for all graph sizes. A Fibonacci addition inequality bounds every nonconstant fiber and proves strict uniqueness of the Lucas-plus-one basin. Direct exhaustive Python and separately implemented C++ tests compared every source and output state through n=19 and n=21, respectively. The uniform claim rests on the proof rather than finite tests.

value.rationale: The odd ring is the minimal natural nonbipartite family excluded from previously counted bipartite open-NOR cases. Complete individual-basin information is a natural phase-space invariant not determined by recurrent-state counts. The cyclic Fibonacci factorization computes each labelled attractor basin directly from its zero-run geometry and proves a sharp unique largest attractor with asymptotically vanishing attraction probability. The result answers a motivated all-size classification question, not an arbitrary small parameter slice.
